params.decision: Fixed before the run (2026-10-15; design: Danyil). Positive control: on the cells where both lenses have the bridge first among the entities, the oracle names the bridge at least 15 points more often than its distractor (question-clustered paired bootstrap 95% CI above 0); otherwise it does not read bridges here and the rest says nothing. (a) On the cells where neither lens has the bridge first (layers 28/36/44, three positions), the oracle names the bridge at least 15 points more often than its distractor, CI above 0. (b) On the questions whose answer flips under exp14's J++ bridge swap on the cue phrase, at layer 44 at the last word or -1, the oracle names the swap target (the distractor) in at least 30% of the swapped reads and more often than in the clean reads (paired CI above 0). Verdict: (a) and (b): "the oracle reads the bridge where the lenses miss it, and follows the state the answer uses". (a) without (b): "the oracle names the bridge on lens-blind cells but does not follow the swap; it may re-solve the hop from the question the activation encodes". Not (a): "no evidence the oracle sees the bridge where the lenses miss it" (a null, if the positive control works). Reported beside every rate: the share of other questions' bridges named, and the reads of the mean activation.
